terms.gloss: a space of time, a period
evidence: Cic. Arch. 1: spatium praeteritī temporis (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 30: tertiō spatiō, in the third period (class period); spatium studiōsum, study period
terms.comment: Often with temporis. A school period is a spatium too: tertiō spatiō, in the third period (Traupman 359).

terms.gloss: time; in the plural, the times, a period
a period of life; an age, an era
evidence: Cic. Sen. 33: suaque cuique partī aetātis tempestīvitās est data

phrases.latin: ā sōle enim exortō ad exortum ejusdem incipientem tōtum id spatium ūnīus diēī nōmine appellāre
phrases.english: (the Babylonians) call the whole period from one sunrise to the next by the name of one day

sources: Lewis & Short: spatium · Lewis & Short: tempus · Lewis & Short: aetas
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 30, 77, 88, 359.
